chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan (Al-Halabi) from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man is struck on his head and his tongue becomes heavy, the letters of the alphabet are presented to him; whatever he fails to articulate clearly from the speech, the blood money is due as qisas (compensation) for that.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or compensation for injury/death

ai.seo_question: How is the blood money calculated for a tongue injury that affects speech clarity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes a precise, empirical methodology for assessing 'defect of letters' (nuqsan al-huruf) by testing the victim's articulation against the Arabic alphabet. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on objective, measurable criteria for diyah, distinguishing this specific injury from general speech impairment by linking compensation directly to the loss of distinct phonetic capabilities.
